velociraptor-mongoliensis.prompt: Create a portrait-oriented 4:5 museum-grade naturalistic paleoart illustration for a children's dinosaur atlas (ages 5-14), scientifically cautious and non-graphic. Scene: Late Cretaceous Djadokhta Formation, Mongolia, at the edge of red sandstone dunes as a light dust gust begins. Use a strong diagonal composition: one Velociraptor mongoliensis in the lower-left foreground, quarter-turn side view, and one Protoceratops andrewsi in the upper-right midground. Both animals must be completely visible from snout to tail tip with every limb and foot readable, separated by a large safe distance, alert but not attacking. Velociraptor: small roughly 2 m feathered dromaeosaur, narrow toothed non-beak snout, folded feathered forelimbs with small three-fingered hands, long stiff banded feathered tail, one clearly raised second-toe sickle claw on each foot, athletic but not giant. Protoceratops: sheep-sized hornless basal ceratopsian, parrot-like beak, modest solid skull-attached frill, low quadrupedal stance, long visible tail, non-hoofed toes; absolutely no large horns or ornate spikes. Warm ochre and muted slate palette, natural light, readable silhouettes, child-friendly quiet tension. No contact, no wrestling, no chasing, no wounds, no blood, no carcass, no roaring monster pose, no extra limbs or digits, no cropped tails, no text, no labels, no watermark. Do not imitate any named artist.

tyrannosaurus-rex.prompt: Create a portrait-oriented 4:5 museum-grade naturalistic paleoart illustration for a children's dinosaur atlas (ages 5-14), scientifically cautious and non-graphic. Scene: latest Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation floodplain at cool misty dawn, with a shallow wet meadow, low flowering shrubs, ferns and scattered conifers. Compose vertically: one adult Edmontosaurus annectens in the lower foreground turns its head while pausing at the meadow edge; one adult Tyrannosaurus rex is fully visible in the upper midground at a brush line, also stopped. Keep clear open ground between them and show both entire bodies from snout to tail tip with all feet visible. Tyrannosaurus: massive deep skull, deep torso, extremely small forelimbs with exactly two fingers on each hand, two powerful grounded hind legs, three-toed feet, long heavy tail; no allosaur horns, no oversized arms. Edmontosaurus: large crestless hadrosaur with a broad low duck-billed skull, no tube crest, deep torso, quadrupedal-capable grounded limbs, low restrained fleshy midline ridge along neck/trunk and tiny restrained rear tail spike row, full tail and feet. Quiet ecological awareness rather than combat, cool teal-gray and russet palette, strong depth and readable silhouettes. No pursuit, no attack, no bite, no contact, no wound, no blood, no carcass, no roaring, no extra limbs or fingers, no cropped tails, no text, no labels, no watermark. Do not imitate any named artist.

tarbosaurus-bataar.prompt: Edit this existing portrait paleoart image while preserving the exact river-separated composition, lighting, landscape, full-body framing, and the distant Tarbosaurus. Correct ONLY the foreground Saurolophus angustirostris anatomy. Replace its current unicorn-like forehead horn with a scientifically cautious Saurolophus skull: a broad low duck-billed muzzle and ONE short solid spike-like crest that grows continuously from the REAR TOP of the skull and angles distinctly backward, nearly following the skull roof. It must not be vertical, conical, detached, nasal, or Parasaurolophus-like. Keep exactly two forelimbs, two hind limbs, four grounded feet, and one complete stiff tail, all separated and uncropped. Exactly two dinosaurs total. No attack, blood, carcass, text, labels, watermark, or named-artist imitation. Naturalistic museum paleoart for ages 5-14.

allosaurus-fragilis.prompt: Edit this existing portrait paleoart image while preserving the exact channel-separated composition, lighting, landscape, full-body framing, and foreground Allosaurus. Correct ONLY the background Camarasaurus lentus anatomy. Make the Camarasaurus head visibly larger and characteristically SHORT, DEEP, and BOXY with a blunt broad muzzle and large nasal region; make the neck COMPACT, THICK, and only moderately long, not a long slender generic sauropod neck. Keep a deep robust torso, level or low shoulders, exactly four sturdy columnar legs with visible grounded feet, and one complete medium non-whip tail. Smooth back only: no spines, armor, plates, hump, or osteoderms. Exactly two dinosaurs total, spatially separated. No chase, blood, carcass, text, labels, watermark, or named-artist imitation. Naturalistic museum paleoart for ages 5-14.
